title: Dolores del Río's birth chart
metaDescription: Dolores del Río's chart, computed from a sourced birth date: Sun at 10.9° Leo. Birth time unknown, so no houses or rising sign.
lede: The Sun stands at 10.9° Leo, in domicile — the planet in its own sign, running on home rules. Of everything the chart can be read for without a birth time, that is the loudest single fact in it.

blocks.title: Where the Sun actually stood
blocks.text: Leo, but precisely: 10.9°, second decan, 10°–20°, under Jupiter in the triplicity scheme. The tradition kept these divisions because thirty degrees is a long street.

blocks.title: Closer to the ground
blocks.text: For the fast movers, Mercury was at 3.4° Virgo, Venus was at 18.3° Leo, Mars was at 22.6° Cancer. Read together: a mind that trusts the measured and the checked; taste that runs toward the vivid and the immediate; drive that moves on certainty and current.

blocks.title: The angles that hold
blocks.text: Start where the chart is tightest — Venus opposition Saturn, 0.1° of separation. The scheme reads an opposition as an axis to walk, not a fight to win: the chart keeps both ends lit. Behind it, Venus sextile Pluto at 3.0°, and Saturn trine Pluto at 3.1° — both still well inside the orbs this site uses. Each angle here was measured at every hour of the civil day and held; whatever the missing clock said, this geometry was in it.

blocks.title: What the angles build
blocks.text: Mars stands apart from every major angle the day held — the tradition reads an unaspected planet as a voice that speaks on its own schedule, unmodulated by the rest of the chart.

blocks.title: The classical map
blocks.text: Of the seven planets the classical scheme judges, four sit in a sign it has an opinion about. The Sun in Leo at 10.9° is in domicile — the planet in its own sign, running on home rules; Mercury in Virgo at 3.4° is in exaltation — the tradition’s honoured-guest placement, working at its best; Mars in Cancer at 22.6° is in fall — the tradition’s uphill placement, strength earned rather than given; Saturn in Aquarius at 18.2° is in domicile. Condition, not character: that is all the dignity table ever measured.

blocks.title: The shape of the whole
blocks.text: Tallied where the signs are certain — 9 placements whose signs hold for the whole day — the chart gives fire 4, water 2, air 2, earth 1, and fixed 3, mutable 3, cardinal 3 across the modes. Fire weights a chart toward initiative — starting, asserting, spending energy to find out what happens. Saturn and Uranus were retrograde — the optical reversal the tradition reads as review — energy turned over before it is turned out.

blocks.title: The Moon is genuinely open
blocks.text: The Moon crossed from Aries into Taurus during that day at the birthplace, travelling 12.2° between one midnight and the next. A birth time would settle it in a second; there isn’t one. So the Moon stays unnamed here — the alternative is a guess wearing the clothes of a fact.
